text:
jon: running a quick heat-check on fused+paged flash variants. ran seq len sweep (128 -> 65536) across A100/H100/L40S with bursty arrivals. seeing weird throughput dips at mid-long seqs. anyone else?
rina: saw similar on H100 earlier, thought it was driver power cap. did you capture clock/power traces? :thinking_face: 
jon: yes, attached nvml snapshots. power drops line up with kernel swap events. but the KV-evictor also spikes right before.
matt: hmm can you paste the perf command? I want to run the same harness.
jon: sure, used the usual bench harness with pinned streams:
```
./bench_attention --model=llama-13b --variant=fused_paged_flash --device=a100 --seqs=128,512,2048,8192,32768,65536 --bs=1,4,8,16 --burst=on --collect=nvml,nsys,memtrace
```
jon: raw summary: A100 throughput falls ~22% at seq 8192 bs8, H100 falls ~30% at seq 2048, L40S more stable but lower baseline.
kevin: did you also capture kernel-level times? i.e., kernel name mapping.
jon: yes, top kernels: flash_forward, paged_merge, kv_evictor_sync. nvprof snippets: 
```
Kernel                                         Time(ms)   Calls
flash_forward                                 11.4       320
paged_merge                                   3.2        310
kv_evictor_sync                                0.9        310
```
rina: `kv_evictor_sync` at 0.9ms seems small but it's sync'd frequently during bursts -> adds jitter. maybe it's a blocking cudaStreamSynchronize we didn't notice.
matt: also check memcpy times for prefix cache loads. If warmed incorrectly, memcpy spikes with larger seqs.
jon: good call. memcpy shows a few 1.5-3ms spikes correlated with evictor. stack trace points to `kv_prefetch_async` fallback to sync when free memory < threshold.
kevin: that fallback is the suspect. our hysteresis threshold is aggressive: `if free_mem < 0.12*total then sync fallback`. maybe with thermals the effective free_mem fluctuates and we flip-flop.
rina: what about thermals? GPU clocks from nvml show a dip ~200MHz right before throughput drop on H100. could be thermal throttle or power-budget governor reacting to hot spots.
jon: interestingly, power draw also briefly dips 60W for ~150ms. timeline: burst arrives -> paged_merge + prefetch -> mem pressure -> evictor runs -> nvml power dip -> kernel fallback -> throughput drop.
kevin: so sequence: memory pressure -> evictor -> thermal/power governor reaction -> kernel behaviour flip -> throughput regresses. two levers: reduce eviction flip-flop, or reduce power/thermal shock.
matt: suggestions: 1) add small async eviction backoff + jitter to avoid synchronized evict events across streams. 2) bump prefetch window sizing to reduce frequent fetches. 3) cap concurrency during burst (limit concurrent streams) as temporary mitigation.
jon: tried a micropatch: add 150ms randomized delay in evictor when recent_eviction_count > 3. retest on H100: drop reduced from 30% -> 8%, power dips less frequent.
kevin: nice. can you paste the quick diff? we need to formalize in kvcache policy.
jon: diff snippet: 
```diff
-kv_evictor_sync(...){
-  if(free < threshold) sync_evict();
-}
+kv_evictor_sync(...){
+  if(free < threshold){
+    if(recent_evictions > 3){ sleep(rand_ms(50,150)); }
+    queue_async_evict();
+  }
+}
```
rina: we need metrics for false positives: did delaying evictor increase OOM risk?
jon: no OOMs in 2000 runs, but tail latency slightly higher for some tiny sequences because prefetch deferred. still net throughput win.
kevin: next steps: 1) add telemetry event for evictor backoff so console can surface. 2) run long 24h soak across P and T variations. 3) attempt variant where prefetch uses progressive chunk sizes to avoid big memcpy spikes.
matt: I'll own progressive-chunk experiment. jon, can you add evictor telemetry? kevin, can you own soak on H100 farm?
jon: ack. I'll push PR with telemetry + flag `kvcache.evictor_backoff_ms` default off for now.
bench-bot: deploy queued: `PR#1874` -> eng-runtime/testbench (run: nightly-thermal-suite).
jon: thanks, plz tag me on results. :thumbsup:
